_readme: Who each company is, for the Introduction tab: a short blurb, the parent's own site in China
(or global) and its US site where one exists, and a slot for a representative photo of one of
its outlets in China. LINKS ARE PROVIDED AS-IS. Any link outside the USA is untested by this
project and should be treated at the reader's discretion — the site warns of this beside every
such link. PHOTOS are not shipped: `photo` names a local file under map/img/ that must be an
image the project has the right to use (licensed, or an official press image with permission);
until one is added the tab shows a neutral placeholder. Never hotlink a copyrighted storefront
photo. `photo_credit` is shown beneath the image when present.

mixue.name: MIXUE
mixue.blurb: The world's largest F&B chain by store count — nearly 60,000 outlets — built on rock-bottom prices (an ice cream cone under a dollar) and a franchise-supply model that sells ingredients to its franchisees. Its crowned Snow King mascot is unmistakable. US entry began in 2025.

chagee.name: CHAGEE
chagee.blurb: A fast-growing premium tea brand (literal name Bawang Chaji) positioned as a China-rooted answer to Starbucks, known for its osmanthus-oolong lattes and minimalist branding. It listed on Nasdaq in 2025 and opened its first US stores the same year.

luckin.name: Luckin Coffee
luckin.blurb: China's largest coffee chain, which overtook Starbucks in China on volume and app-first, low-price convenience — remarkable given it was delisted after a 2020 accounting fraud and rebuilt. It opened its first US stores in New York in mid-2025.

miniso.name: MINISO
miniso.blurb: A variety retailer of affordable design-led goods and licensed-character (IP) merchandise, with a Japanese-inspired aesthetic despite its Guangzhou roots. It is this project's largest US presence and the most established here.

popmart.name: POP MART
popmart.blurb: The blind-box designer-toy phenomenon behind Labubu and other collectible figures, sold through staffed stores and unmanned “Robo Shop” vending kiosks. Its US footprint has grown fast across malls nationwide.

haidilao.name: Haidilao
haidilao.blurb: The hot pot giant famous for over-the-top service — free manicures, noodle-dancing performances, birthday songs. Its overseas arm, Super Hi International, runs its US restaurants; it has been in the US since 2013.

heytea.name: HEYTEA
heytea.blurb: The brand that popularised the “cheese-foam” and fresh-fruit tea category in China, positioned at the premium end. Its US stores cluster in Chinese-American neighbourhoods; it publishes no US store locator, so its footprint here is assembled from public records.

cotti.name: Cotti Coffee
cotti.blurb: Founded in 2022 by the two executives ousted from Luckin, and aimed squarely at their old company: Cotti undercuts on price and has expanded worldwide at extraordinary speed on a franchise model. Its US growth is quiet and franchisee-led, with no public US locator.

taier.name: Tai Er
taier.blurb: A Sichuan sauerkraut-fish (suancai yu) restaurant brand from the Hong Kong-listed group Jiumaojiu, known for its stylised branding and single signature dish. Its US presence is small and new — San Mateo, San Jose, Flushing, LA.

chabaidao.name: ChaPanda
chabaidao.blurb: A large Chinese fruit-tea chain (Chabaidao) that listed in Hong Kong in 2024. It entered the US in 2025 trading as “TeaByDo”, with only a handful of stores so far.

nayuki.name: NaiSnow
nayuki.blurb: The US arm of Nayuki (Naixue), a premium Hong Kong-listed tea-and-soft-bread chain, trading in America as “NaiSnow”. It entered the US in late 2025 and is expanding quickly across New York and into New Jersey.

juewei.name: Juewei
juewei.blurb: A Shanghai-listed braised-snack chain (“duck neck” and other marinated items) with tens of thousands of outlets in China. Its US presence is delivery-forward and tiny — it trades here as Juewei Yabo, Jue Wei Kitchen and Jue Wei Food.

yangguofu.name: Yangguofu
yangguofu.blurb: One of China's two dominant malatang (build-your-own skewered hotpot soup) chains, founded in Harbin in 2003. It began a registered US franchise programme in 2024, trading as YGF, and is expanding across the coasts.

fishwithyou.name: Fish With You
fishwithyou.blurb: A Chinese fast-casual chain built on one dish — Sichuan sauerkraut fish (suancai yu) over rice — founded in Beijing around 2016 with thousands of outlets in China. In the US it trades under several names (Fish With You, YONNY, Wei's Fish) with per-store sites rather than one locator.

yangs.name: Yang's Braised Chicken Rice
yangs.blurb: A braised-chicken-over-rice brand that was one of the earliest Chinese chains in America (trading since 2017) but is now in retreat — most of its US restaurants have closed. Included because it is here, and because a chain opening and closing without a first-party list is exactly what a census exists to catch.
